$comment: Generic secret shapes only; this deployment's own identifiers are not published.
$copyRootComment: Root files copied verbatim from the private tree (round-9 security, 2026-09-19). `.npmrc` used to be one of them: a registry file is where an auth token lands (`//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=`), and the scanner had no pattern for one, so a token added to the private root would have been published on the next sync. The public tree gets the fixed two-line file in template/ instead, and this list is for files whose content is only tooling settings.
$patternsComment: The token classes this repository actually holds (round-9 security, 2026-09-19): npm automation (the release workflow's NPM_TOKEN), Resend (mail), a Telegram bot token, and a PEM smuggled into a single line as \n-escaped text, which the multi-line pattern above cannot see. HEY's own API keys (2026-09-30): an account key `hey_` and a partner key `heyp_`, each 43 url-safe characters; a digit is required so a long snake_case identifier such as a foreign-key name is not taken for one. An Ory API key `ory_<two letters>_…` and a CoinGecko API key `CG-…` (S2, 2026-10-16). An Anthropic key `sk-ant-…` (the AI key this deployment holds), the OpenAI project, service-account and admin keys, an AWS access key id `AKIA`/`ASIA` (the S3 settings) and GitHub's OAuth, user-to-server, installation and refresh tokens `gho_`/`ghu_`/`ghs_`/`ghr_` (2026-10-16): `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}` needs twenty letters straight after `sk-`, so it saw none of the first two. An EVM private key (full audit 2026-10-24, SECURITY-8): 0x and 64 hex characters assigned to a private, attester, signer or deployer key variable, the shape HEY_SHIP_ATTESTER_KEY has; an assignment only, so a transaction hash or storage slot of the same shape in a fixture is not taken for one. A value assigned to one of the secret environment names packages/config and .env.example declare (2026-10-25): sixteen or more key characters with a digit after `NAME=`, after `NAME:` in quotes, or alone on its line after `NAME:` (YAML), so a provider key with no shape of its own (twitterapi.io, Bitquery, Uniswap, Blockscout, a session or webhook secret) is caught where it is pasted beside its name; a reference such as `process.env.NAME` or a placeholder or test value (change, replace, example, your, test, fake, fixture) is not taken for one.
